 Final Jeopardy: Well-Known Americans (11-16-26)
 The Final Jeopardy question (11/16/2026) in the category “Well-Known Americans” was:
 His TIME magazine obit says, “He grew gross & paunchy & wore a bulletproof vest … He was 48” & “died like a rich Neapolitan” 
 4x champ Will Goree , Will Goree , a teacher from Austin, TX, won $97,500 last week. In Game 5, he’s up against: Kali Sluyter , a director of prospect development orig. from Muskegon, MI; and Josh Luiza , a CFO from Annapolis, MD. It’s “all eyes on Will today” because a 5th win has been elusive thus far. 
 Round 1 Categories: For Their Birthday – Kissy Face – 3 Letter Responses – That’s the Ball Game – Between Heaven & Hell – A Southern Dandy Category
 Kali found the Jeopardy! round Daily Double in “Kissy Face” under the $600 on the 3rd pick of the round. She was the only one on the board with $800. Kali bet $800 and said my brother. That was WRONG. 
 In Matthew 26 he says, “Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast” show 
 WHO IS JUDAS? 
 Kali finished in the lead with $4,000. Josh was in second place with $3,600. Will was last with $2,800. All clues were shown. 
 Round 2 Categories: Possessive Lit – The Navy – 2026 in Science – Contestants Call for the Hits – Less-Common Double Letters – A Dandy Southern Category
 Will got the first Daily Double in “Possessive Lit” under the $2,000 clue on the 2nd pick of the round. He was in the lead with $4,400, $400 more than Kali in second place. Will made it a true Daily Double and was close but close is WRONG.
 In this Jodi Picoult novel with a 3-word title that Cain didn’t say, Anna was conceived as a bone marrow match for Kate show 
 WHAT IS “MY SISTER’S KEEPER”?
Will said My Brother’s Keeper 
 Will got the last Daily Double in “2026 in Science” under the $2,000 clue on the 5th pick of the round. In last place with $1,600 now, he had $4,000 less than Josh’s lead. Will bet $2,000 and tried titanium neutron objects. That was WRONG.
 The Vera C. Rubin Observatory detected more than 11,000 new asteroids, including hundreds of these bodies, TNOs for short show 
 WHAT ARE TRANS-NEPTUNIAN OBJECTS? 
 Kali and Josh finished in a tie for the lead with $9,200. Will was next with $8,000. All clues were shown.
 NONE of the contestants got Final Jeopardy! right.
 WHO IS AL CAPONE? 
 Last week, we had the St. Valentine’s Day Massacre in the final round. Today it’s Al Capone, the man believed to be responsible for it. Capone died on January 25, 1947, a week after his 48th birthday. TIME had a lot to say about him but I thought this one sentence summed his life up the best: “While one great American statute had helped make him, another–the income tax law–broke him.” 
 Alphonse Capone obituaries, including the New York Times as well TIME, claimed he was born in Naples, Italy, which may account for the Neapolitan reference. It’s just wrong. His parents came to the USA from a town near Naples, Italy in 1893. Capone himself was born in Brooklyn, New York on January 17, 1899. 
 Will came up with Marlon Brando. He lost his $7,000 bet and finished with $1,000. Gollee-eee! This was one time I was hoping that Will bet bupkus!!
 Kali drew a blank. She lost $7,000 and finished with $2,200.
 Josh tried Howard Hughes. He bet and lost it all, and that made Kali Sluyter the new Jeopardy! champ.
 A triple stumper from each round:
 ($1000) A scandal in Naples! In 1798 this Navy man’s mistress Emma Hamilton hosted his lavish 40th birthday party at her husband’s crib
 A DANDY SOUTHERN CATEGORY ($2000) 1,100 miles east of Tierra Del Fuego, this island visited by James Cook in 1775 sounds like an area for the dandy in the Jeopardy! round 
 More clues on Page 2 
 2 years ago: NONE of the players got this FJ in “19th CENTURY AMERICA”
 : It caused rich amusement that the name of this president, whose wife didn’t allow dancing, was similar to that of a dance show 
 WHO IS JAMES K. POLK?

 Loose lips sink ships. Will consistently gave wrong responses, missed two DDs, yet fought back and got into the game. With $8K and both opponents at $9200, he should have bet $0 or maybe $1201 and hoped both would go all-in (which one did do). Cost himself a 5th win.
 I got clobbered on the DDs and Final (I said Fitzgerald) but overall wasn’t terrible. Thought for sure someone would get the Sessions/Webster clue, same for the neck scarf, and am 100% shocked no one knew the OT king’s mines or the 70-degree Navy vessels. Good grief! (Same for the FJ from 2 years ago–no one got it but it was semi-obvious to me.) Also knew the Joe Jackson and McCartney songs. JJ is a big favorite. $5600 in all.

I mean, this was the way that we all read it. No, Capone stood at 5 Ft. 10 In. We cry foul!
